text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- British Minister of State Derek Fatchett who was on a few-hours official visit to Lebanon said there would be no change in the British foreign policy with Labour Party in power.
- Japanese Red Army guerrillas awaiting trial in a Lebanese jail will celebrate the 25th anniversary of an anti-Israeli operation in which 24 people were killed.
- The Bank of Lebanon issued certificates of deposit dated May 30 to commercial banks worth 99 billion Lebanese pounds.
- Prime Minister Hariri stormed out of parliament in a clash over soaring government borrowing but then easily survived a vote of confidence taken after he left.
- National carrier Middle East Airlines received a leased A321 Airbus as part of its programme to rehabilitate and expand.
- Lebanon's central bank is seeking to sell Credit Libanais, a medium-size bank it acquired in 1989.
- Israeli shelling on villages in the central sector of south Lebanon.
- The board of Lebanon's Byblos Bank has decided to increase share capital to 200 billion Lebanese pounds ($130 million) from 66 billion.
- Japanese Red Army accused Lebanese officials of taking money to arrest five of its guerrillas in February.
